skills.name: build

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

Use when the user mentions copilot-setup-steps, copilot setup steps, or wants to configure the cloud agent environment.

20. // across calls. The substance of the abstraction is the spec function

27.     // determinism, injectivity) is structural — a property of `spec_gva_to_gpa`,

29.     pub open spec fn inv(self) -> bool {

31.     }

1. # View Design: `hal::platform::microvm` (target: `gva_to_gpa`)
2. 
3. ## Abstract Resource
4. 
5. To callers, the in-scope facet of this module is the MicroVM platform's
6. **guest-virtual → guest-physical address translation**: a *pure, total,
7. deterministic* function from a `usize` address to a `usize` address. On the
8. MicroVM platform the guest runs in a flat, identity-mapped address space, so
9. this translation is the **identity map** (`GPA == GVA`).
10. 
11. Crucially, this facet carries **no mutable state**. `gva_to_gpa` is a free
12. function (`#[inline(always)] pub fn gva_to_gpa(gva: usize) -> usize`), not a
13. method on `Platform`, and it reads/writes no globals. There is therefore no
14. caller-observable *state* to model — only a caller-observable *mathematical
15. map*. The honest View for this scope is a **stateless (unit) View** whose
16. content is a single pure translation function plus the algebraic properties the
17. caller relies on.
18. 
19. > This is a deliberate, documented outcome of the methodology — not an
20. > oversight. Inventing fields here (e.g. memory bounds, a translation table,
21. > `Platform`'s internals) would fail the substitution and minimality tests
22. > below. See **Rejected Alternatives**.
23. 
24. ---
25. 
26. ## View Struct
27. 
28. ```rust
29. /// Caller-visible abstraction of the MicroVM platform's address-translation
30. /// facet. The translation `gva_to_gpa` is a pure, stateless function, so this
31. /// View carries no fields: there is no mutable abstract state a caller observes
32. /// across calls. The substance of the abstraction is the spec function
33. /// `spec_gva_to_gpa` and its properties, defined below on this type.
34. pub struct MicrovmTranslationView {}
35. ```
36. 
37. The reusable abstraction lives **on the View type** (per view-design: "no extra
38. `pub spec fn` on `impl MyType` beyond `inv`/`view`; put helpers on the View"):
39. 
40. ```rust
41. impl MicrovmTranslationView {
42.     /// Abstract guest-virtual → guest-physical translation as a mathematical
43.     /// map over addresses. On the MicroVM platform the guest address space is
44.     /// flat and identity-mapped, so this is the identity. Addresses are modeled
45.     /// as `nat` (raw, non-negative machine addresses live in spec world).
46.     pub open spec fn spec_gva_to_gpa(self, gva: nat) -> nat {
47.         gva
48.     }
49. }
50. ```
51. 
52. `spec_gva_to_gpa` is `open` because **identity is the caller-relevant contract**
53. on MicroVM (the caller depends on the result equaling the input to walk distinct
54. frames). Hiding it would force callers to re-derive injectivity/monotonicity
55. they are already told to assume.
56. 
57. ---
58. 
59. ## Well-formedness Invariant
60. 
61. ```rust
62. pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
63.     // The translation facet is stateless: there is no internal bookkeeping to
64.     // constrain. Well-formedness of the abstraction (totality, determinism,
65.     // injectivity) is structural — it is a property of `spec_gva_to_gpa`, a
66.     // total Verus spec function, not an invariant over mutable fields.
67.     true
68. }
69. ```
70. 
71. The properties a caller cares about are **not** state invariants; they are
72. intrinsic to the spec function and exposed as caller-facing facts (next
73. section):
74. 
75. - **Totality** — `spec_gva_to_gpa` is a total Verus spec fn; defined for every
76.   `gva: nat`. (Mirrors the exec function never panicking / always returning.)
77. - **Determinism / purity** — a spec function is by construction a function of
78.   its argument only. (Mirrors "same input ⇒ same output, no side effects".)
